notes.summary: Polity gives about 2–3 questions. Focus on the making of the Constitution, important Articles, sources of borrowed features, key amendments, and the President, Parliament and constitutional bodies.

concepts.title: Making of the Constitution
concepts.body:
• Constituent Assembly first met on 9 December 1946; Dr. Rajendra Prasad was its permanent President.
  • Dr. B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.
  • Constitution adopted on 26 November 1949 (now Constitution Day) and came into force on 26 January 1950 (Republic Day).
  • The Preamble begins 'We, the people of India'. The words socialist, secular and integrity were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976).

concepts.title: Important Articles
concepts.body:

32Right to constitutional remedies ('heart and soul' — Ambedkar)
51AFundamental Duties
72Pardoning power of the President
112Annual Financial Statement (Union Budget)
280Finance Commission
324Election Commission
352 / 356 / 360National / State (President's rule) / Financial emergency

concepts.title: Key amendments and numbers
concepts.body:
• 42nd (1976): 'mini-constitution'; added Fundamental Duties.
  • 44th (1978): Right to Property removed from Fundamental Rights.
  • 52nd (1985): Anti-defection law (Tenth Schedule).
  • 61st (1989): Voting age lowered from 21 to 18.
  • 73rd / 74th (1992): Panchayats / Municipalities.
  • 86th (2002): Article 21A, right to education.
  • 101st (2016): GST.
Numbers: Eighth Schedule lists 22 languages; minimum age for President is 35; Rajya Sabha maximum strength is 250.

varieties.name: Article ↔ subject
varieties.how: Recall the Article table; questions name the subject or the number.

varieties.name: Borrowed features
varieties.how: Pair each country with its feature; DPSP = Ireland and Fundamental Duties = USSR are the most asked.

example.q: The idea of Directive Principles was taken from which constitution?
steps: DPSP came from the Irish Constitution

varieties.name: Amendments and institutions
varieties.how: Link each amendment number to one change; link each body to its Article.

example.q: Which amendment lowered the voting age from 21 to 18?

tips: Article 32 is the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution in Ambedkar's words.
42nd Amendment is the most-asked amendment; learn its three Preamble words.
traps: The Constitution was adopted on 26 Nov 1949 but came into force on 26 Jan 1950.
Fundamental Duties came from the USSR, not the USA.
Rajendra Prasad was President of the Constituent Assembly; Ambedkar chaired only the Drafting Committee.

questions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution abolishes untouchability?
questions.solution:
Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.
Memory hook: 17 = 'end of untouchability' — the middle of the equality block 14–18.

questions.q: The Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution were inspired by the constitution of:
questions.solution:
Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) were added by the 42nd Amendment, inspired by the constitution of the former USSR.
Memory hook: Soviet = duty to the state.

questions.q: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution?
questions.solution:
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee. Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the President of the Constituent Assembly.
Memory hook: Ambedkar = Architect (both start with A).

questions.q: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called which Article the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
questions.solution:
Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) lets a person go directly to the Supreme Court to enforce Fundamental Rights.
Memory hook: 32 teeth protect the mouth; Article 32 protects your rights.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years?
questions.solution:
The 61st Amendment Act, 1988 (in force 1989) reduced the voting age to 18.
Memory hook: say it as one line — 'Sixty-one made eighteen vote'.

questions.q: The concept of the Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from:
questions.solution:
The Concurrent List (and joint sitting of Parliament) was borrowed from Australia. Canada gave the idea of a federation with a strong Centre.
Memory hook: Australia = All share (Concurrent).

questions.q: Which amendment added the words 'socialist', 'secular' and 'integrity' to the Preamble?
questions.solution:
The 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'socialist', 'secular' and 'integrity'. It is called the 'mini-constitution'.
Memory hook: 42 = the 'mini-constitution' that touched even the Preamble.

Article 360 deals with Financial Emergency. National Emergency is Article 352.
Memory hook: 360° covers all the money — Financial Emergency.
